messages:
maria_g: Heads-up — customer reported a large vectors/sec drop starting ~2024-12-23T14:30Z after the autoscaler/optimizer rollout. Tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec down ~60%. Repro steps below.

support_bot: alert: embeddings-throughput-drop severity=warning; link: https://alerts.redwood.com/alert/9876 :rotating_light:

maria_g: Repro steps I used: 1) POST /v1/embeddings with mixed-length batch (64 items, short+long mix) 2) model rwd-embed-3b-quant 3) observe vectors/sec ~200 vs baseline ~600.

maria_g: Minimal curl used:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \n -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{"input":["hi","this is a longer sentence ...","ok","another long text ..."],"model":"rwd-embed-3b-quant"}'
```

ryan_k: Can you confirm there are no 400s/422s or dim mismatch errors in the client logs? Any auth/billing noise?

maria_g: No client-side 4xx. Runtime logs show intermittent "dimension reshape fallback" and small batches emitted:```text
[2024-12-23T14:31:02Z] kernel_select: reshape mismatch -> fallback_variant selected
[2024-12-23T14:31:02Z] batch_coalescer: emitted small batch size=8
```

kevin_z: That "fallback_variant" is from the new kernel optimizer we rolled 2 days ago. It triggers when per-sample seq-lens vary and a reshape would be required. It can force per-sample handling and prevent batch-level kernel. Tagging @sre_oncall.

maria_g: I reproduced locally: forcing uniform input lengths returns vectors/sec to baseline immediately. Mixed lengths => saw small batches and the reshape logs.

sre_oncall: Node metrics for pool-embed-prod at 14:31 show GPU util fell to 22% while queue depth (pending_requests) climbed to ~320. That's consistent with many small batches not saturating GPU. infra-bot forwarded a billing/auth blip at 14:29 but it was transient and unrelated.

infra-bot: billing-alert: transient auth 401 spike (14:28-14:30) from tenant-id xyz - impact: token auth retries increased briefly.

kevin_z: Hypothesis: batch coalescer merge-window was reduced from 20ms -> 5ms in canary to lower latency. For mixed-length traffic that made more small batches and exposed the reshape fallback. Plan: revert merge-window for canary to 20ms and monitor.

ryan_k: Quick test: set env RWD_BATCH_MAX_WINDOW=20ms on a canary slot and enable debug flags `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel,coalescer`. Also capture per-request trace ids.

maria_g: Running that now. Results: with 20ms window vectors/sec ~620, GPU util ~78%, no reshape fallback. With 5ms window vectors/sec ~210, GPU util ~18%, reshape fallback appears ~1/3 batches.

kevin_z: Good repro. Please attach trace ids for one failing and one healthy request so we can diffs kernel selection.

maria_g: Trace IDs: trace-01ab (failed, small-batch) and trace-01ac (healthy). Snippet:```text
trace:trace-01ab kernel_select: candidate_variants=[fast,quant] chosen=quant reshape_needed=true
trace:trace-01ac kernel_select: candidate_variants=[fast,quant] chosen=fast reshape_needed=false
```

ryan_k: Actionable mitigations: 1) revert merge-window to 20ms in canary ASAP 2) warn customers about mixed-length payloads in release notes 3) longer-term: group by seq-len in coalescer or support zero-pad grouping to avoid reshape.

sre_oncall: I'll watch canary and promote rollback if vectors/sec recovers. Assigning runtime ownership to @kevin_z for a fix and follow-up.

maria_g: I'll update the customer with repro + mitigation steps and attach the traces to the support ticket.

kevin_z: Filed bug RWD-5821 and PR #4023 to undo the aggressive merge-window change and add a coalescer metric for reshape-fallbacks. Will follow up in the morning. :thumbsup:

maria_g: Thanks — closing loop once canary shows stable numbers.
